comparator.name: Astronomy
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define a mandatory 150-EC Astronomy major and a 30-EC free minor. The pathway below accounts for the complete 180 EC and preserves the genuine 30-EC minor space rather than silently selecting either of the two optional deepening minors or inventing an unrelated minor. The Astronomy and Astronomy Instrumentation and Informatics deepening minors are available choices, not formally distinct routes through the bachelor; no formal route is therefore assigned.

exception.reason: The University of Groningen programme is a full disciplinary Astronomy degree. Its compulsory 150-EC major combines calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, numerical methods and statistics with mechanics and relativity, electromagnetism, quantum physics, thermal physics, waves and optics, observational astronomy, planetary science, stellar and galactic physics, radiative processes, advanced electrodynamics, astrophysical hydrodynamics, the interstellar medium, laboratory skills and a 15-EC astronomy research project. UCR offers useful mathematics and computation plus adjacent study in Earth systems, imaging and robotics, but no Astronomy or Astrophysics course, no sustained physics core and no astronomical-observation or experimental-physics laboratory sequence. A UCR programme assembled from mathematics, computing and Earth science would be a coherent quantitative pathway, not a defensible Astronomy comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 regulations account for the full 180 EC as a mandatory 150-EC Astronomy major plus a 30-EC free minor. Year one comprises 60 EC in calculus, differential equations, electricity and magnetism, introductory and observational astronomy, programming and computational methods, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, and physics laboratory skills. Year two comprises 60 EC in complex analysis, planetary science, numerical methods, stellar and galactic physics, two sequential quantum-physics courses, radiative processes in astrophysics, statistics, thermal physics, and waves and optics. The remaining major comprises advanced electrodynamics, astrophysical hydrodynamics, the interstellar medium, and a 15-EC bachelor research project; the 30-EC minor completes Year three. The live programme page likewise presents a research-oriented, mathematically and physically grounded Astronomy bachelor totaling 180 EC.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant foundations in calculus, differential equations, matrices, numerical algorithms, transforms, signals, systems and statistics. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming supplies Python and computational problem-solving; DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision and DISDATA312 Robotics apply mathematical and computational methods to imaging, kinematics and motion. ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth includes a broad introduction to geophysics, ENSENVI213 Earth System Science Tools uses quantitative modelling, and ENSSUST111 Climate Change and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address adjacent Earth and energy applications. The workbook nevertheless contains no course in astronomy, astrophysics, planetary science, stellar or galactic physics, cosmology, radiative processes, interstellar-medium physics or astronomical observation. It also contains no sustained sequence in classical or relativistic mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics, thermal or statistical physics, waves or physical optics, advanced electrodynamics, or astrophysical hydrodynamics, and no experimental-physics or astronomy laboratory progression. HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory is explicitly biochemical and molecular, not physical or astronomical. No available sequence culminates in an equivalent 15-EC Astronomy research project. The mathematical and computational strengths therefore cover supporting tools, not the defining Astronomy curriculum.
